content.label: Great program. Serves as a great collector of tasks and project info.
This a great app to keep all your task and events in one place.

I still find adding to dos to Things being 2 more taps away than other to do apps

Most want a frictionless way to add our todos and to add a schedules todo I have to tap on when and later scroll down to write when I want it to be scheduled

Ideally it should be able from the todo name to parse ‘in June 12’ ‘on June 12’ ‘on Jun 12’ ‘June 12’ or similar strings to speed up adding to dos

Also I do not have an iPhone with action button but I plan to get one and I would suggest to add a shortcut for the action button to add a to do

title.label: WHY NO ABILITY TO ADD PICTURES TO TODO????

content.label: I love this app and have for years, however I can’t give it 5 stars because of the lack of an option to add a picture to the todo. Otherwise it’s a very great app. Still no ability to add pics to tasks. I don't understand why.
I have used many productivity, tracker app but nothing comes close to Things. Not only it is solid with all the features you can think of or need but also so well designed and developed.

This is easily my favorite todo list app. It’s clean and straightforward design make it a joy to use. I do have a few minor gripes, however. Tags are not very accessible on mobile. First, they don’t display in the list with your tasks. Instead, the area that the task originates is displayed. The ability to show tags in the list would be very helpful. It would also be nice to be able to create new lists based on filters… such as having a “Work - Today” list that lists everything tagged work with a date set to today.

title.label: The Most Important App in my Life

content.label:
I wanted to leave a formal review as a thank you to the makers of this app. This has been my life-tracking app for years now.

Incredible, thank you for making it a one time purchase. Thank you for constantly updating.

I wish there was a way they can make it compatible with fonts in the app so we could have a easy way to change fonts instead of using a font keyboard, cool if it was comparable with fonts and Apple fonts that's already installed on the computer! Other then that this app is the best I love it and have used it for at least 3 or 4 years!!!

I really love the layout of this app. It’s exactly what I’ve been looking for the keep me organized for work and personal life. I really want to be able to share his with my spouse so that we can work on these lists together and be on the same page. I’m not sure if sharing is a function that’s available and I can’t figure it out, or if it’s jus not supported. Either way, I’d expect to have some way to collaborate in the app for how expensive this app is.

title.label: 最新版apple watch里面的things没有了

content.label: watchos7

If you think you might import you reminders from reminders app into thing you would think it would leave copy on reminders app but no it deleted them from reminders app leaning me screwed  thank for nothing

Integration with Apple shortcuts is bad, with limited examples and unclear documentation. If I want to do something as simple as "show me project x when I arrive at location y," it shouldn't take hours of fiddling to accomplish that.

title.label: Love things and please expand widgets

content.label: Great app and well worth the paid version. I’m hopeful you will expand the widget offerings to include a broader range of sizes and shapes. I’d like a widget that can run top to bottom covering one half of the screen on either the left or right and spanning up to the entire screen. I find that I have multiple lists running for different tasks and the current widgets are limiting for arrangement on the Home Screen.

Not intuitive. I can’t believe I spent money o something that supports GTD. I can’t figure out how to move something to a project. This is terrible. This is not flexible. This assumes you actually have outcomes and projects laid out .awful.

title.label: Most Powerful To Do App on the Market

content.label: What an incredible app. Use it daily to keep it all straight. Have noticed a huge decrease in distraction and stress because I know Things is keeping me on track.
This is exactly the app i’ve been looking for.

I was looking for a replacement for Microsoft To Do since it was being buggy and slow. Things is great! The interface is clean and easy to use, and so far it has all the features I’ve wanted. I love that it’s a one-time fee, too. No complaints so far!

I’ve been using Things app for over 10 years. I bought it on my phone and then iPad and then Mac computer. It is the most important app on my phone, especially for getting things done and not forgetting important task. The Things app team are always one of the first to adopt Apple’s new software pushes. They’re always cutting edge. And I am so thankful they are not subscription based like everyone else these days. Thank you Things team.

title.label: One of my top favorite apps!

content.label: I almost never leave reviews, but I seriously LOVE this app. It’s simplicity makes it approachable, and my productivity is high while my cognitive load and stress is way more in check. As a busy mom of two, I think this is one of my most favorite apps ever for helping me stay organized and not having a million things floating around in my head!
I’d give Things five stars if they would EVER fix the rigid repeating task rule that refuses to allow you to complete a repeating task early. It’s been broken for years and years.

title.label: Great app. Feels like it was made by Apple.

content.label:
Works wonderfully. I’ve never encountered a bug in either this or the desktop app. I use them together to organize all of my college work and I don’t know how I would remember anything without them. In particular, I like how quickly new tasks can be added. On my Mac I can just press a hotkey to create a new task on the fly, from within any app. This lets me capture tasks as quickly and seamlessly as possible before I forget about them.

Things has a good balance between functionality and simplicity. I’m prone to spending too much time tinkering with task tracking apps, to the point where just managing tasks becomes a task in itself. The simplicity of Things helps prevent this and thereby reduces the amount of maintenance required. The easier the system is to maintain, the more likely I am to stick to it.

It takes a little reorienting to start thinking about tasks in a way that harmonizes with Things, but once you get the hang of it, it’s very powerful. It’s nice to not have anything slip through the cracks.

title.label: Reminder Badge Fatigue - New System Needed

content.label:
Updated:

I believe the badge system has been useful, but we now need a persistent system to help keep us on track. Things is a great resource, but Intend to forget about what’s due or get distracted and don’t get back to a task that is due at a certain time. 

I’d like to see Things add a persistence reminder with a very loud tone that goes off every 1, 5, or 10 mins. This is a system found in the “Due” app, but I prefer Things’ interface. I would drop Due if Things added this feature of persistent reminders. 

Old Feedback:

I'm super excited to see individual time alerts. The UI is much more refined and concise with internal menus and shortcuts, such as the new drag + add button. I've waited a very long time for this upgrade, but I fear it could have come much earlier; however, the developers needed an all new feel to re-justify the price tag. -1 Star for the last point made.

I have been with Things since the beginning (7 years?). On three occasions over the last two years I have asked whether Things will modify their data security system to allow for encryption that cannot be decoded by its employees. The response has been “in the future”. Unfortunately the confidential data and metadata that is in my Things database is too important for me to leave it to Cultured Code’s Human Resources policies that limit what people have access to my data. I can no longer wait for the fix. I am today switching to OmniFocus which has full no-knowledge data encryption at rest as part of its platform. I do not like the OmniFocus UI as much as I like Things. However data security is more important to me.

Not too much, not too little, just what you need to keep in track of your life. This has been ine of the best purchase apps to keep my life in check and not forget things. Truly efficient in terms of moving things around when plans change. Really recommend it to people that just want to organize their lifes without too many features added to the app.
My first blush with this app and it has not disappointed me.  Loving it so far!!!

title.label: Got it because of Vision Pro support - use it everywhere

content.label:
I didn’t know that I needed a new task manager.  I was using an iPhone app.  When I saw the VisionPro support and reviews for Things I gave it a shot.  I really like the clean interface but I love that I have my tasks with me everyone on Macs, iPads, phone and VisionPro.  

It’s not a plan if you don’t have it with you.

Feature request: be able to tap the circle next to a Project on any screen (ex. Today) to mark it as completed just like you can a regular todo item. 

 Currently you have to tap it & open the project, then tap the circle again. Not difficult to do but it seems counterintuitive to be able to do that function on one screen but not the other.

title.label: Simple, but powerful if you want more of it

content.label: I tried many apps trying to create a to-do list, and I knew what I was looking for, but each app I tried either was too simple or very complicated or it would work only on iPhone but not on iMac, and I wanted to work on both devices with the data synchronized thru the cloud. When I found this “Things” app it was exactly what I was looking for, a simple interface, common sense buttons and instructions; but powerful if I wanted more from it, capable to synch thru the cloud, and it would work on my iPhone, my iMac, my iPad and my iWatch. I totally recommend this app to anyone looking for a simple and powerful app to manage projects as to-do lists.

Amazing app. Has literally made staying organized fun. And makes you want to add stuff. I’m going on a trip in a few days and I just typed everything I need to bring. I’ve never done that before in my life! Down to what’s going in my car, my suitcase, my backpack! 

The PLUS button everywhere (on widgets especially) paired with Inbox feature is best for quick notes to self and brain dumps. 

The built in tutorial is the best part. I just finished going through it step by step. One of the last tasks was to write a review. So here I am. Bravo THINGS! 👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼

Only issue, I wish there were a bundle price for multiple devices. I payed the $10 for phone and am doing 14 day trial on Mac. Haven’t added it to the iPad. Like that its pay what you need. Wish there were a bundle discount.

The combination of reading Getting Things Done and then installing this app to help me get organized has been life changing and I’m not exaggerating. This app has boosted my productivity and more importantly increased my peace of mind. I accomplish more and all while feeling like nothing is falling through the cracks. I’m able to combine work and personal items while tagging them appropriately and keeping everything that’s important visible to me. If you are a fan of Getting Things Done then this is the app for you.

The simplicity of this app keeps you focused on productivity and not on customization options.  I don’t know how I would live without this app as it keeps me organized in my work, personal life and all around.  By no longer keeping any to-do lists in my head, it has helped me reduce my stress and get better sleep.  Crazy how much a simple app can change your life! Have it for all my devices and it is worth every penny.

This app has a nice Ul and is very intuitive but it does not have end-to-end encryption of your data, which leave it exposed! This is unacceptable in 2024. While the app is nice, this drawback makes it unusable to someone who values security and online privacy. The developers need to add end-to-end encryption ASAP! Once this must-have functionality is implemented, I will gladly amend my rating.
So thoughtfully made and clean. A delight to use.
Love this App overall just wish pictures can be attached to notes and task.

I hesitated to buy this but couldn’t be happier. I first tried todoist (free) but found that it didn’t sync properly with my calendar and the customer support feature didn’t work. So I went with Things for my phone and iPad. It’s great — very intuitive and perfect for managing my to do list and calendar. Very easy to use. Glad I coughed up the $ and got it!

Very well designed and polished.

One feature that would make it more useful is the ability to set reminders/deadlines for subtasks. Would be 5 stars if it had this feature.

I’ve been using Things for years now and it’s an essential part of my productivity. Without being distracting, or time intensive, it allows me to keep track of everything I have going on and remind me of all my recurring tasks like taking out the garbage and changing my air filters. 

Ever so often I have tried out the latest new thing or looked into old apps to compare and things continues to be the perfect balance between deep and feature rich, and clean to look at it. It’s honestly amazing! 

My one wish is that there were the capability to nest projects inside other projects like todoist. But honestly, there are many work arounds that make it not a deal breaker at all.
This app, along with its Mac counterpart, is one of the sexiest, most-intuitive apps on the market. It’s fast, easy-to-use, and robust in terms of features. I highly recommend it.

It’s been years since any major updates, I’d love to see more customization themes, (not big fan of all the colors) but that is not such a dealbreaker, what I really want to see on a future update is a way to prioritize tasks like the Eisenhower Matrix :)

I’ve been using this app for almost three years and it’s been fantastic, but I do have a suggestion that I think will make this app even better. When you look at your list of to-do’s, the app only lists each out in a single line. This is the case for notifications as well. Sometimes when I write a to-do, it’s over a sentence long and it would be nice to read all of it in one go without having to tap on it to expand it just so I can read it all. 

Any to-do longer than approximately five words is cut off and an ellipses is added to the end. This is even worse when you have a deadline set because it shows that label on the far right side of the to-do, taking up that much extra space. Something as simple as allowing text to use two lines instead of one would be wonderful. Hopefully this can be changed in an update. What inspired me to write this review was how I’d be notified of a to-do and I could complete it right from that banner BUT, I’d still end up opening the app to confirm all what I wrote instead of completing the to-do right from the Notification Center. Other than all of this, it’s a great app.

title.label: The best app on my Mac and phone for 13 years

content.label: Simple and excellent. Great product and focus. Thank you!

title.label: Where has this been all my life?

content.label: I’ve struggled a lot over the years to find something that just WORKS. So many other apps have so much clutter that I really don’t need on a day to day basis and the stock app was too simple. Things 3 is a minimal but powerful tool. I am very excited to explore more of it but it’s been 2 hours since I downloaded and I have organized and input all my to dos and my brain feels better already. I think that’s pretty telling!

title.label: Really good app but I believe is missing something

content.label: The app is overall good. I really like the visibility and the mappings of all the buttons and other aspects that are part of the app. However, I think one thing that could be added is to add an “undo”, this will improve feedback to the user as if they mistakenly click on a task and they have not yet done/completed it they can quickly undo it. Instead of having to go around or adding it again.  Or maybe this is a personal issue but I do believe this would be a good addition to the app and improve feedback for the user. Lovely app overall though!!!

Big fan of the app, and have used it for years. With the addition of stage manager on iPad, however, the ability to drag and drop new to-do’s from the bottom right corner is no longer functional. When I reached out to the dev, they stated that it’s not possible to just move that button to adapt to the change resulting from stage manager and refuses to change (blaming Apple, rather than adapting). Since this drag and drop was a large part of my work flow, I’ll likely be changing to another app, unfortunately.

What am I ever going to do if this app ceases to be?

I like the reoccurring tasks. I like the divided sections. I like that it’s pretty simple. 

It was expensive to have to buy separately for each platform I use, but I’ve been using it happily for 3+ years with no complaints. 

I love Things.

Pros:
Pay once and you own it. Great, intuitive UI. Easy to use.

Cons:
Using the app in multiple platforms is 10$ for th iPhone, $50 for macos, and the iPad app is a separate purchase. All this, and you can't even attach an image to a task / list item.

--

I wish when I'm adding multiple options to a list that it would remember which heading I last interacted with. On the iphone, after a while when the list gets long, it gets difficult to add items to the end of the list. Instead I have to make an item, and then drag it to the bottom of the list
This app has single-handedly saved me hours and hours of time, and I have only had it for about a week. Give it a try, you will not be disappointed. It is well worth the price.

Things is essential in my life for remembering things. You can set up one-time or periodic reminders quickly for those must happen tasks. 

Or for those someday-maybe stuff you can keep items on your todo list for years. 

There’s checklists and a logbook to look back. 

Buy it - it’s worth it. You’re with it!

title.label: iPhone app is amazing! Desktop version needs refinement

content.label: I love the animations and responsiveness. Dragging the “+” button is a nice trick. Full-featured app, which brings joy to the process of organizing life’s tasks. My only complaint is that the desktop version, while much more expensive, feels like it’s missing that design elegance— e.g., no draggable + button, and the UI feels a bit bland. I was expecting more for the $50 cost.

title.label: No calendar events in today widget 😔

content.label: The one feature that I am missing from this app.
